topic: PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For signed-distance boundary-discontinuity regression, impose Lipschitz side means and a common lower local-mass modulus m(h) along the entire boundary, and target the boundary CATE curve under expected sup loss. A polynomial horn whose cross-section at inward depth u has width proportional to u^(kappa-1) has tube mass proportional to h^kappa, not h^(kappa-1). Balancing Lipschitz bias h with stochastic size sqrt{log n/(n h^kappa)} yields the horn rate (log n/n)^(1/(kappa+2)). More generally, prove uniform consistency exactly when some h_n decreases to zero while n m(h_n)/log n diverges; an exponential horn should force order-one risk. Construct a mass-adaptive estimator and matching same-class lower bound, then determine honest uniform-band limits. The rd2d R, Python, and Stata boundary-design workflow and its Ser Pilo Paga replication are genuine consumers. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Turn the thickness criterion into a two-sided minimax theorem for arbitrary declared moduli, including data-driven bandwidth choice, a legal packed lower family, and honest adaptation or a precise impossibility result. EARLY KILL TEST: Drop if the horn mass exponent is wrong, if the claimed iff fails for a monotone legal modulus, or if existing boundary or support-estimation theory already gives this exact signed-distance causal criterion and matched adaptive inference.

open_problems.open_problem: For every geometrically realizable monotone two-sided tube-mass modulus m(h), determine the sharp expected-sup minimax risk for a Lipschitz signed-distance boundary CATE curve and the exact consistency frontier.

source_refs.claim: Establishes identification, uniform estimation and inference, and minimax lower bounds for distance-based boundary CATEs under regular positive-density and Gram conditions, not arbitrary vanishing tube-mass moduli.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: Derives pointwise minimax rates under vanishing random-design density, ranging from power rates for regular variation to logarithmically slow rates under severe degeneracy.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Gaïffas

source_refs.excerpt: The full P_NP result is converse-only: no full-class achievability is claimed.
Develop the OEQ into a positive companion theorem for one named density-modulus or angular-balance class

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature treats either a regular boundary-indexed causal curve or one-dimensional/pointwise degenerate random design, while the banked CausalSmith result matches upper and lower risks only on a fixed Gram-regular class and is converse-only on its broader class. An arbitrary m changes the effective sample size, the local-polynomial Gram scale, and which packed alternatives are legal. The presolve exponential-horn claim also needs correction: any fixed m(h)>0 at every h admits a sufficiently slowly shrinking h_n with n m(h_n)/log n diverging, so an exponential horn gives a logarithmically slow but vanishing risk; order-one risk needs zero common local mass at some small scales or another uniform entropy/noncompactness obstruction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A same-class upper-and-lower minimax theorem identifying risk by an oracle functional such as inf_h{Lh + sqrt(log N_B(h)/(n m(h)))}, with an iff consistency corollary, the rate (log n/n)^(1/(kappa+2)) for m(h) comparable to h^kappa, a logarithmic-rate exponential-horn corollary, and a precisely stated order-one regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the causal estimand, the geometry-driven motivation, the expected uniform-risk formulation, and the empirical distance-based workflow.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Boundary designs identify an effect curve -> signed-distance smoothing makes local geometry control information -> regular thickness hides severe support depletion -> characterize the complete thickness-indexed estimability frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate local-polynomial bias and least-favorable regression bumps to a regularly or severely varying local design mass, and match the resulting information equation with a minimax lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its rate equation is the closest pointwise analogue of replacing ordinary h-mass by an arbitrary boundary tube-mass modulus.

method_exemplars.technique: Use boundary-indexed signed-distance local-polynomial linearization, uniform empirical-process approximation, and a manifold-indexed minimax packing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the causal and expected-sup proof components that must be rebuilt when the Gram matrix degenerates at the m(h) scale.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a signed-distance boundary CATE estimator whose location-specific bandwidths are selected from empirical one-sided local counts and which attains a uniform oracle risk over unknown thickness moduli.

source_refs.claim: Uses local polynomials and Lepski selection to adapt jointly to unknown local design density and regression smoothness at one query point.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Gaïffas

source_refs.claim: Selects the neighbor count locally and obtains near-minimax pointwise regression rates governed by unknown ball-mass growth under doubling measures.
source_refs.author: Samory Kpotufe

source_refs.claim: Provides boundary-sensitive bandwidth rules for distance-based BATEC estimation but retains regular positive-density and uniform Gram conditions.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.excerpt: At the theorem bandwidth h_n=a_n, the winsorization level is B_n=a_n^(-1/3).

open_problems.why_unsolved: The adaptive regression papers control one query point or generic nearest-neighbor regression, whereas the causal target requires simultaneous control over a continuum of known boundary points and both treatment sides. The first proof step that changes is local invertibility: empirical scalar-mass bounds must become uniform lower-eigenvalue bounds for two random local-polynomial Gram matrices. A selected, location-dependent bandwidth then enlarges the empirical-process index and creates denominator-failure and bias-comparison events absent from the banked fixed-bandwidth estimator. The targeted web scan found no result combining unknown thinning, two sides, boundary-uniform expected-sup loss, and a matching adaptive lower bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit empirical-count, k-nearest-neighbor, or Lepski local-polynomial BATEC estimator with a boundary-uniform oracle inequality over a union of declared modulus classes, plus a same-union lower bound identifying any unavoidable adaptation logarithm.

writing_exemplar.why: Its practical bandwidth narrative and whole-boundary causal target make the unknown-thickness problem immediate to applied readers.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Applied boundary RD reports an entire effect curve -> a common bandwidth presumes uniformly abundant observations -> local thickness varies and is unknown -> select scales from empirical one-sided mass with a sharp uniform guarantee.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare local-polynomial fits across scales using an empirical-design norm and Lepski thresholds tied to random local variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already adapts to unknown scarcity; the destination replaces one query by two sides uniformly along a boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Choose k(x) from observed neighbor radii and prove rates directly from local ball-mass growth rather than a known global dimension.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same observable-radius device can make a boundary bandwidth respond to unknown local tube mass.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple multivariate Lipschitz-indexed and multiplicatively separable empirical processes uniformly to Gaussian processes with explicit rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The selected location-bandwidth grid needs process control beyond the fixed-scale maximal inequality used by the prior proposal.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether honest variable-width uniform bands for the boundary CATE curve can adapt to an unknown thickness modulus, and characterize the weakest design-separation condition if unrestricted adaptation is impossible.

source_refs.claim: Constructs pointwise intervals and uniform BATEC bands by Gaussian approximation under regular positive-density and Gram conditions, not vanishing unknown thickness.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocio Titiunik, Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: Shows that unrestricted honest rate-adaptive bands fail over Hölder unions and that self-similarity restores adaptation in its regression, density, and white-noise settings.
source_refs.author: Adam D. Bull

source_refs.claim: Derives honest bias-aware inference for nonparametric regression and RD and formalizes the coverage cost of data-driven adaptation.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesár

source_refs.excerpt: Unknown-smoothness adaptation, boundary bands, and weak separation remain outside the closed theorem.
The measurable same-class upper bound and frontier-order interval length remain open research objects.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The existing BATEC band proof uses uniform covariance nondegeneracy, while classical impossibility results concern unknown function smoothness rather than an unknown but observable sampling-thickness law. Under thinning, the studentized variance, correlation metric, and selected bandwidth all vary along the boundary; the first fragile step is a uniform Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration bound when local Gram matrices approach singularity. Because thickness is partly learnable from X, a smoothness-style impossibility cannot simply be imported: the needed lower bound must construct two design classes that remain statistically indistinguishable at the scales controlling band width, or else a positive result must exploit conditional-on-design calibration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a conditional or multiplier-bootstrap band with uniform asymptotic coverage and expected local width matching the modulus-specific minimax rate over a stated class, or a two-design ordered-modulus lower bound proving that honest adaptation requires an explicit separation condition.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames why simultaneous BATEC inference matters and how geometry enters the feasible uniform band.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The estimand is an entire boundary effect curve -> heterogeneity claims require simultaneous uncertainty -> thin regions determine local variance and feasible width -> establish honest variable-width bands and the limits of adapting them.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian anti-concentration, multiplier bootstrap, and bootstrap-calibrated data-driven resolution selection for suprema.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A thickness-adaptive boundary band has a non-tight supremum and random tuning, the two features this proof architecture is built to handle.

method_exemplars.technique: Use worst-case bias, honest critical values, and modulus-of-continuity efficiency bounds for nonparametric RD inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the causal-inference template for a sharp band-width benchmark or an adaptation lower bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Strongly approximate the boundary-indexed studentized local-polynomial process and simulate its supremum for feasible uniform bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the exact regular-thickness band argument whose Gram and covariance steps must be made thickness-adaptive.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize which primitive density and support-geometry conditions make a two-sided tube-mass modulus imply uniform signed-distance local-polynomial Gram coercivity, including interior cones, polynomial cusps, and horns.

source_refs.excerpt: Add a primitive lemma: which local-mass and density hypotheses imply the uniform Gram lower bound?
a verifiable sufficient-condition corollary for polygonal and smooth GIS partitions

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted proposal treats local mass and Gram coercivity as distinct assumptions, and its reviewers explicitly rejected silently identifying them. A total tube-mass lower bound can concentrate mass at unfavorable signed-distance radii, leaving higher-order polynomial moment matrices nearly singular. The first proof step therefore needs subannulus or radial-balance control, with constants derived from support geometry and the density, before any stochastic estimator theorem can use m(h) as its sole information index.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp sufficient-condition or necessary-and-sufficient theorem translating cone, cusp, density, and radial-balance parameters into explicit lower eigenvalue moduli for every declared local-polynomial degree, with computed h^kappa moduli for polynomial horns.

writing_exemplar.why: Its estimator is formulated through signed-distance moment matrices, making the primitive-to-operator bridge the natural problem statement.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Local-polynomial BATEC estimation needs invertible signed-distance moments -> abstract Gram assumptions are hard to verify in geographic designs -> tube mass is interpretable but does not ensure radial balance -> derive checkable geometric coercivity conditions.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze local-polynomial normal equations in intrinsic coordinates and derive their conditioning from local manifold geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired statement likewise converts neighborhood geometry into quantitative moment-matrix behavior.

method_exemplars.technique: Turn reach and embedded-boundary regularity into nonasymptotic sampling-mass bounds and geometry-faithful hard families.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest proof pattern for translating primitive support geometry into local statistical information.

literature_map:
1. Keele and Titiunik's geographic-RD work motivates treatment-effect curves along boundaries and warns that scalar distance can change the local comparison.
2. Sawada, Ishihara, Kurisu, and Matsuda (arXiv:2402.08941) study multivariate local-polynomial boundary RD and contrast it with distance reduction.
3. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu's location-based paper (arXiv:2505.05670) gives pointwise and uniform BATEC inference from the full bivariate score under regular density.
4. Their 2026 Journal of Econometrics distance-based paper (arXiv:2510.26051) gives identification, uniform rates, bands, and minimax lower bounds under regular density and Gram conditions.
5. Its irregular-boundary n^(-1/4) phenomenon concerns distance-induced geometry and misspecification, not an arbitrary vanishing tube-mass modulus.
6. Gaiffas (2005, Mathematical Methods of Statistics, arXiv:math/0410354) derives pointwise minimax rates under degenerate random designs, including logarithmically slow regimes.
7. Gaiffas (2007, ESAIM, DOI 10.1051/ps:2007023) gives a local-polynomial Lepski estimator adaptive to unknown local design density and smoothness at one point.
8. Gaiffas (2007, Statistics & Probability Letters, arXiv:math/0509634) obtains spatially varying sup-norm rates and an inhomogeneous confidence band when the density remains positive.
9. Gaiffas (2009, Statistica Sinica, arXiv:math/0610113) treats weighted uniform loss with vanishing design density, but not a two-sided causal boundary curve.
10. Guerre (2000, Journal of Multivariate Analysis, DOI 10.1006/jmva.2000.1901) adapts to arbitrary unknown design by conditioning and selecting a random neighbor count.
11. Kpotufe (2011, NeurIPS, arXiv:1110.4300) makes pointwise kNN regression adapt to unknown local ball-mass growth.
12. Bull (2012, EJS, DOI 10.1214/12-EJS720) and Hoffmann-Nickl (2011, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/11-AOS903) characterize obstacles to honest adaptive bands over nested smoothness classes.
13. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1303.7152) provide anti-concentration and multiplier-bootstrap tools for data-selected uniform bands.
14. Armstrong and Kolesar (2020, Quantitative Economics, arXiv:1606.01200) provide bias-aware honest nonparametric and RD inference with modulus-based efficiency comparisons.
15. No located paper occupies the exact intersection of two-sided signed-distance BATEC estimation, an arbitrary common vanishing mass modulus, expected-sup minimax loss, adaptive bandwidths, and honest bands; a fixed positive exponential modulus implies logarithmically slow consistency rather than order-one risk.
prior_proposal_map:
Accepted stat_bdd_uniform_log_penalty/v1 was the dominant adjacent source; its README, proto core, writeup, and reviewer files angle0_v1 through angle0_v7 were inspected.
Its banked result leaves full-P_NP achievability open and confines the matched frontier to a fixed Gram-regular P12 class.
Reviewer angle0_v2 yielded the primitive local-mass-and-density to Gram-coercivity problem.
Reviewer angle0_v6 yielded operational finite-packing and interior-cone/GIS sufficient-condition directions.
Reviewer angle0_v7 yielded the named density-modulus or angular-balance companion with a faster rate and matching obstruction.
The square-support angular marked-Poisson construction is the closest donor for a legal polynomial-horn lower family, but its proposed exponential order-one transfer fails the fixed-positive-modulus kill test.
Downgraded stat_transport_boundary_overlap_calibration_frontier/v1 supplied boundary-depletion and honest-interval analogies while leaving measurable attainment and frontier-order interval length open.
Downgraded stat_spectral_hte_bands/fixed_error_minimax_width supplied the closest causal uniform-band construction and records adaptation and boundary bands outside its closed scope.
Failed stat_prte_ot_boundary_adaptation/v1 was inspected as an adaptation warning: its cross-class converse failed because class separation forced product total variation to one.
